acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Lizardfolk family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Saurian Tyrant, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Back-Sail Warcourt Sovereign (Sovereign) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A full back-sail crest, ceremonial feather-and-hide mantle, stone tail-club, and war paint across the entire plated body create an unmistakable sovereign mechanism.

Signature mechanic: Five Marks of the Sail: five painted panels on the full back-sail map to arena markings. Bone calls Scouts across one line, Reed braces Warriors, Obsidian raises a Spineback gate, Skull orders a Chieftain quarter, and Stone commits the Tyrant's own tail-club through the surviving marks. The ceremonial feather-and-hide mantle is tied once beneath each panel. After the selected learned pattern resolves, its tie stretches across the dorsal gap; cutting it folds that sail panel, erases the mark, and removes the command. With two panels left, the mantle falls and the Tyrant must plant before every tail sweep.
battlefieldDuty: Transform a five-mark hunting ground through a full back-sail crest, ordering lower forms until each cut mantle tie lowers one sail section and removes a phase rule.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe construction: T1 Scout uses whistle holes in the bone spear, a vented hide wrap, tail streamers, and vane strips tied to existing scale rows and planted feet; T2 Warrior may add reed panels and vanes to its low crest; T3–T5 may add hollow flutes and pressure vanes only along mature dorsal spines and mantles.
Motion exposes pressure through the T1 spear whistle and tail line, the T2 shield flex, and T3–T5 coherent streamlines that leave a still pocket behind the loaded dorsal ridge.
counterplay: Use the selected lower-form response, reach the exposed dorsal tie, and cut it; every collapsed panel permanently removes one command and opens that section of the arena. Affinity signal: T1 Scout aligns its bone spear, hide-wrap vane, and tail streamer down one lane while a planted foot stays still; T2 Warrior aligns low-crest vanes and reed slats, while T3–T5 expose the silent dorsal gap from the lee.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only pale scales without flutes, vanes, and directional pressure
Glow-only wind treatment without a force route and still center
Ordinary feathers or tail balancing presented alone as Wind affinity
Floating or turbulence that hides planted reptilian footwork
identityInvariants: An upright forward-leaning reptilian body keeps clawed hands and feet, a long counterbalancing tail, a crocodilian or iguana-like head, and an escalating dorsal ridge.
Swamp green, mud brown, moss, and ochre are punctuated by warning-bright orange, red, or yellow throat and crest colors.
Scale, bone, obsidian, hide, river reed, ordinary mud, and feather remain separately legible materials.
Paint, bone piercings, trophy skulls, woven shields, and feather headdresses accumulate without obscuring natural plating.
Tail angle, crest posture, dorsal plates, hands, and planted feet preserve the direction and recovery of each attack.
telegraph: One body-painted sail panel rises, the matching mantle tie pulls taut, its arena mark is exposed, and the chosen lower form assumes its known posture.
